hook_text: The Sun is a star. So why does it look so much bigger than all the others?
clip_script: A soccer field in Polokwane. On one goal line: a marble. That is the Earth. Now walk. Past the halfway line. Past the other goal line. Keep going. Here is the Sun: a ball as big as you. That is the real difference! The Sun is a star, a giant ball of hot gas, more than a hundred times wider than the Earth. It only looks small because it is so far away. It is our closest star.
visual_style: Whiteboard soccer field with a tiny marble labelled Earth at one goal post and a huge yellow ball labelled Sun far away at the other end, then the Sun drawn as a glowing ball of gas with heat and light arrows pouring out.
mood: Bold and amazed, like discovering something enormous hiding in plain sight.
pacing: What the Sun is made of, then how big it is, then how far away it is, with the soccer field model as the big reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build your own marble model of the Earth and the Sun.
